Definition: from the base of G3674 and a derivative of the alternate of G138 (meaning a crowd); association together, i.e. a multitude:--company.
BiblicalUsage: Hómilos means a crowd, a throng. It never actually appears in the Greek New Testament as it stands, so there is no passage to point to — the word lives in the lexicon, not in a verse.
TheologicalSignificance: I take hómilos honestly: a word with no verse behind it, and I will not pretend otherwise.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
